Title_bis 'Agta' is not a mold word (no other card uses it), but the body says 'agup-op ... fungi nga mokaon sa pagkaon', the corpus-standard word, so the fact is intact.

Title_bis 'Asin' (salt) looks like a typo for 'aso' (smoke); the body correctly says toxic smoke, bad for air and lungs.
Imaginary sphere, infinite radius, celestial bodies projected as seen from Earth.

Can't evacuate -> close doors/windows, stay inside, keep ash out.
Each hormone has one specific body part it affects = target organ.
Wrap nail with wire, connect battery, attracts iron while current flows.
Protected by Philippine law, illegal to catch or hurt.
Title 'Uga' is a typo of 'ugat'; the body is correct — one-way valves in leg veins stop backflow under gravity.
Straight back = more lung room; slouching squishes lungs.
Thylakoid membranes, light energy, ATP/NADPH/oxygen — identical.
Pods only on real cacao trees, cared for.
All figures identical (1.64 x 10^24, 32.69 g, 12 g/mol) and the method is the same.
Stirred = homogeneous, unstirred = heterogeneous with sugar sinking.
'mobuto' (bursts) is the wrong verb for 'melts', but the same sentence keeps solid->liquid at 24 C and then says 'dali kini matunaw', so melting is restored. Wording worth fixing, not a fact change.

EN 'A dragonfly nymph' vs BIS 'nymph sa tabanog'. 'Tabanog' is Cebuano for KITE — this same corpus uses it that way in ffct-22499, ffct-22630 and ffct-26820 — while dragonfly is 'alindahaw'/'tutubi' in 38 other cards, including this card's own title_bis 'Nymph sa Tutubi'. A Cebuano-only child reads that a kite has a nymph living underwater; the animal is never named correctly anywhere in the Cebuano body.
Object at focal point, reflected rays parallel, no image formed.
Blink vs years, reaction rate = how fast/slow a chemical reaction happens.
'nga kusog' loses the 'all on their own' nuance, but the mechanism (wind or animals carry seeds to the ground) is intact.
Bold red/white stripes as a warning sign that it is dangerous.
Pulleys (polea) raise large sails by pulling ropes.
Both sides of paper, donate or sell instead of throwing away.
Drops EN's 'some' hedge on faster breakdown; plant starch (corn/cassava) vs petroleum is intact.

EN 'Wind spins large blades' vs BIS 'Ang hangin mopapailaw sa dagkong blades'. The spinning step, which is the answer to the card's own question about how a wind turbine makes electricity, is replaced by a light-related non-word and never restored.
Adaptation defined the same way, same scope.
Sturdy front fins used like arms/legs to push across mud.
Big round object, night sky, glowing softly among stars.
Raw cassava substances turn into cyanide when digested; peel and cook thoroughly.
Four types, O universal donor, AB receives from any type.
Current-carrying wire makes its own magnetic field, interacts with magnets.
Silver as old money/coins, valuable, easy to carry.
Air, not a failure of gravity, explains the mixed landing result.
Wood -> wet pulp -> spread into sheets -> pressed and dried.
Michael Faraday, Father of Electricity, for his discoveries.
Dense nucleus with protons/neutrons, electron cloud, >99.9% empty space.
273.15 Kelvin / 273.15 K, both kept exactly.
Same six weather factors, same order.
Millions of tiny hair-tips gripping together beats one big sticky patch.
Called 'flying lemur' but not a true lemur and not a monkey.
Year 2061 kept.

Cold/lukewarm cleans as well; soap and scrubbing (friction) remove germs, not heat.

Volta, voltaic pile, world's first battery with steady current.

'tiki' (gecko) narrows EN's generic 'lizard', but drop-tail, distraction, wriggling and regrowth all hold for it.
Lower stage, click low power lens in, remove slide — same order.
Queen lives years, workers only weeks.
Weathering by heat, cold, water, wind breaking big rocks into smaller pieces.

Opaque wood/stone block light completely, making a clear dark shadow.
4 to 6 km per second, depends on the material.
Sun and wind turn water in wet clothes into water vapor.
'hangin gikan sa habagatan-kasadpan' = wind from the southwest; the word 'monsoon' is dropped but direction and heavy rains are kept.
Dew gives small animals and plants a little water each morning.

Elisha Otis, 1853, safety elevator with a brake.

'nakakat-on og kaon' for 'adapted to eating' is a mild softening; Calauit, Palawan, African giraffes, local leaves all kept.
'mapahait' (sharpen) vs EN 'trimmed'; calcium and beak upkeep are both present.
Monera = bacteria, no true nucleus.
Kids play close to dogs, so easier to be bitten or scratched.
'tuki' is this corpus's Cebuano name for whale shark (6 other cards); plankton and small fish, filtered from water, are kept.
'buto sa langgam' is the corpus's standard phrase for bird bone (8 other cards); fused bones, strong but light, skeleton handles flight.
Sierra Madre blocks Pacific moisture, drier rain shadow over Central Luzon.
Polyaniline/chitosan coatings slow oxidation, prevent rust.
Crepuscular rays named; visible because light scatters off dust and droplets.
Rolling ball passes on its motion; the struck ball moves off.
Campfire warmth from a distance = radiation through air.
Red has the longest wavelength, seen far away and through fog/rain.
100 centimeters in one meter, both times.
Water and salt let current flow; disrupts nerves and heart signals.
Remove pollutants -> environment recovers -> plants and animals return.
Epiphyte, antler-shaped leaves, clings to trees, catches water and rotting leaves.
Force resisting motion; slows rolling or sliding things.
Particles stay close but slide past one another, so liquid flows.

The one fact the card exists to teach (this mosquito also transmits dengue) is never stated in Cebuano; the corpus everywhere else uses 'nagdala', 'mokaylap' or 'nagpasa' for spreading a disease.

EN 'Wind spins large blades' vs BIS 'Ang hangin mopapailaw sa dagkong blades' — 'papailaw' is to light up, not to spin. The spinning of the blades is the mechanism the card teaches and it is never stated anywhere in the Cebuano.
Adaptation defined as the biological mechanism of adjusting to new or changed environments.
Sturdy front fins used like arms/legs to push across mud — kept.
Big round object, usually seen at night, glowing among stars.
Raw cassava -> cyanide when digested; peel and cook thoroughly. Safety instruction intact.
Four types listed; O universal donor, AB universal recipient — direction not reversed.
Current-carrying wire makes its own magnetic field, hence interacts with magnets.
Silver used as money/coins because valuable and easy to carry; title 'Paga' (payment) is terse but not contrary.
Air, not a failure of gravity, explains the mismatched landing; the 'not gravity' clause is preserved.
Wood -> wet pulp -> flat sheets -> pressed and dried; order preserved.
Michael Faraday, Father of Electricity — name and title match.
Dense nucleus with protons/neutrons, electron cloud, >99.9% empty; number unchanged.
273.15 K freezing point, both spellings kept.
All six weather factors listed in the same order.
Millions of tiny hair tips gripping together beats one big sticky patch; contrast preserved.
Not a true lemur and not a monkey; both negations kept.
Year 2061 unchanged.
Segment removed, genes on the missing piece lost — kept.
Seawater denser than freshwater due to dissolved salt; Dead Sea example kept.
Changing number or type of components affects the whole circuit; examples kept.
O3 = three atoms, O2 = two; numbers correct and not swapped.
Cold/lukewarm water cleans as well; soap and scrubbing, not heat. The added word 'friction' does not change the fact.

Body keeps softer belly fur, different-colored top and bottom. 'mas mapusok' for 'paler' and title_bis 'Lumot' (probably a typo for 'lumo', soft — it pairs with the body's 'humok') are wobbly, but I am not confident enough in these words to call the card wrong.
Volta, voltaic pile, first battery with steady current — kept.
Dissolved ionic compound -> free-moving ions -> water conducts; chain intact.
Tail dropped to distract, keeps wriggling, slowly regrows; 'tiki' is the normal Cebuano lizard.
Lower stage, click low-power lens in, remove slide; order preserved.
Queen lives several years vs workers a few weeks; contrast not reversed.
Weathering by heat, cold, water and wind breaking big rocks into small pieces.

EN 'the effort step requires pulling the rope downward' vs BIS 'kinahanglan nimo bunalon paubos ang pisi' — 'bunalon' is to strike/whip, not to pull. The card exists to teach the pulling action of a fixed pulley; the downward direction survives but the action itself is a different thing.
Opaque wood/stone block light completely -> clear dark shadow.
4 to 6 km/s, depends on the material — numbers and units unchanged.
Sun and wind turn water in wet clothes into vapor; evaporation link kept.
Southwest wind bringing heavy rain; 'habagatan-kasadpan' = southwest. 'Unhang' is a typo for 'Unsang' but the question is still readable.
Dew ('yamog') gives small animals and plants a little water each morning.
Viscous resin hardening to a solid in air, described as a physical change.
Mangrove roots and mud filter dirt/nutrients before the sea, keeping coastal water clean and protecting reefs.
Life forms changed over millions of years; many ancient animals gone.
Air is not empty space and takes up room; 'nag-okupar og puy-anan' is an odd word for 'space' but still says air occupies a place, and the inverted-glass example follows.
Elisha Otis, 1853, safety elevator with a brake — name, date, device all match.
Keeping trash out of rivers, beaches, forests protects animal habitats.
Calauit, Palawan; African giraffes eating local tree leaves. 'nakakat-on og kaon' for 'successfully adapted' keeps the fact.
Cuttlebone gives calcium and maintains the beak; 'mapahait' (sharpen) vs 'trimmed' is a minor shade, beak-maintenance fact stands.
Monera = bacteria, no true nucleus; kept.
Kids play close to dogs, so bites/scratches are easier; risk direction preserved.
Eats only plankton and small fish by filtering. 'tuki' is the Cebu regional name for whale shark — regional variation, not an error.
Fused bones = strong but light skeleton for flight. 'buto' instead of 'bukog' for bone is a Tagalog-leaning word choice, but title_bis uses 'bukog' and the fact is unchanged.
Sierra Madre blocks Pacific moisture creating a rain shadow over Central Luzon; cause and effect kept.
Corrosion inhibitors slow oxidation and prevent rust; named coatings kept.
Crepuscular rays visible by scattering off dust and water droplets.
Rolling ball transfers motion, struck ball moves off instead; transfer direction preserved.
Campfire warmth at a distance = radiation through air.
Red has the longest wavelength, visible from far and through fog/rain; claim unchanged.
1 m = 100 cm in both.
Water and salt in the body let current flow, disrupting nerve and heart signals.
Remove pollutants -> environment recovers, plants and animals return.
Epiphyte, antler-shaped leaves, clings to trees, catches water and rotting leaves.
Friction resists motion and slows rolling or sliding objects.
Liquid particles stay close but slide past each other, allowing flow.

EN 'also spreads dengue' vs BIS 'nagapasabot usab og dengue' — 'nagapasabot' means 'means/indicates', not 'spreads/transmits'. The card's core claim, that Aedes albopictus also transmits dengue, is never actually stated in Cebuano (range and cold tolerance are fine).
